sections.h2: Who bills and collects real estate tax in Norfolk?
sections.html:
Two city offices split the work. The Office of the City Assessor sets the value, and the City Treasurer sends the bills and collects the money. City Council decides the tax rate and the due dates each year when it finalizes the budget, according to the Treasurer's real estate tax page.

Norfolk collects on a fiscal year that runs July 1 to June 30. The Treasurer's page says the office bills more than 68,000 taxable parcels every quarter, and bills are mailed at least 30 days before the due date. The Treasurer also collects nuisance abatement liens that come over from Neighborhood Quality, and those carry a 30 day payment window.

Ask the Treasurer or the Assessor for the rate on your parcel before you work out a payoff.

sections.h2: When are Norfolk real estate tax payments due?
sections.html:
Norfolk bills real estate tax four times a year, with due dates on September 30, December 5, March 31 and June 5. A Norfolk owner who sells mid-year can therefore owe a payment that came due only weeks earlier.

QuarterPeriod coveredDue date
1stJuly 1 to September 30September 30
2ndOctober 1 to December 31December 5
3rdJanuary 1 to March 31March 31
4thApril 1 to June 30June 5

Source: City of Norfolk Treasurer. The city sets these dates annually, so check the current bill if you are close to a deadline.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a Norfolk assessment?
sections.html:
Norfolk gives owners two routes, an informal review with an appraiser and a formal hearing before the Board of Review. The Assessor's appeal page lays out both.

  • Informal appeal: call 757-823-1343 to book a conference, in person or by phone, with an appraiser. The window opens when the April notice arrives and closes May 8, or the next business day if May 8 is a weekend.
  • Formal appeal: file with the Board of Review by the last business day of May. The page lists June 1, 2026 as the received or postmarked cutoff for that year.
  • Packet: one original plus five full sets of copies, and a separate application for each parcel.
  • Representatives: an agent needs an original letter of authorization on the owner's letterhead, dated in the same calendar year and notarized.

At the hearing you get five minutes to show that the value is above market or not uniform with comparable homes. Virginia law presumes the assessor is correct, and the taxpayer carries the burden of proof under Va. Code 58.1-3379. An appraisal submitted as evidence must be written for appeal purposes, and for the 2026 cycle the page asks for a July 1, 2026 value date using 2025 sales.

sections.h2: Where is Norfolk, and how does the water shape its housing?
sections.html:
Norfolk is an independent city in southeastern Virginia where the Elizabeth River meets the Chesapeake Bay. Wikipedia gives it 96.41 square miles in total, but only 53.28 of those are land, with 43.13 square miles of water. The city sits at an elevation of about 6.9 feet.

That low ground matters to anyone selling. The 2020 census counted 238,005 residents, and a 2025 estimate puts the figure near 231,013. Tidal flooding days rose from about five in 2000 to roughly 10 to 15 by 2020, and Hurricane Isabel in 2003 pushed a storm surge into the Midtown Tunnel. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers began a Coastal Storm Risk Management project after a 2019 study, and Wikipedia reports a March 2026 estimate of $6.1 billion with completion planned for 2037.

A seller who can hand over an existing elevation certificate or a flood zone letter has a ready answer when a buyer asks about flood risk.

sections.h2: How does flood zone status affect selling a Norfolk house?
sections.html:
Flood zone status can change what a buyer pays for insurance, so Norfolk publishes a property lookup. The city's Flood Zones page explains that zones come from FEMA's Flood Insurance Rate Map and are enforced through Article 3.9.7 of the city zoning ordinance and the Virginia Uniform Statewide Building Code.

The page also points owners to a site called Forerunner, where you can search a property, see flood data and find existing elevation certificates. It lists these zone types:

  • X: outside the 0.2 percent annual chance of flooding.
  • Shaded X: 0.2 percent annual chance, with depths under 1 foot in a 1 percent event.
  • AE, AH and AO: 1 percent annual chance areas, with AE carrying a mapped base flood elevation.
  • VE and LiMWA: coastal areas affected by wave action.

If your house sits in an AE zone, expect the buyer's lender to ask about flood coverage. Either way, the title company still needs the tax lien cleared.

sections.h2: Which Norfolk neighborhoods and employers do sellers hear about?
sections.html:
Norfolk's housing stock is spread across older waterfront neighborhoods and newer revitalized districts. Wikipedia names Ghent, Colonial Place, Larchmont, North Shore, Edgewater and Lafayette Shores among the popular residential areas, plus the historic Freemason district. Berkley, Willoughby Spit and Ocean View have long ties to the water.

The 2024 employer list on Wikipedia puts these names at the top:

  • U.S. Department of Defense, with Naval Station Norfolk described as the world's largest naval installation
  • Sentara Healthcare
  • Norfolk City Public Schools and the City of Norfolk
  • Old Dominion University and Children's Hospital of the King's Daughters

A Navy family that gets orders on short notice may not have time for a repair list, and an as-is sale is one way to handle that.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid tax when a Norfolk house sells?
sections.html:
Unpaid tax is paid from the sale proceeds, because Virginia puts the tax lien ahead of every other lien. Va. Code 58.1-3340 says the purchaser, or the trustee in a foreclosure, must apply proceeds to taxes and levies assessed on the property, and the lien covers penalties and interest too. The treasurer then releases it.

The statute also says the seller's tax liability is prorated by contract, so the purchase agreement should state who covers the current quarter. Virginia adds a grantor's tax of 50 cents per $500 under Va. Code 58.1-802, paid by the seller unless the parties agree otherwise. The clerk of the circuit court collects it when the deed is recorded, with half going to the state and half to the city.

The Treasurer's page also shows what happens when tax stays unpaid. It announced an online-only public auction of two Norfolk parcels for unpaid real estate tax, held under Va. Code 58.1-3975 in June 2026, sold as is with a 15 percent buyer's premium. That is a reminder that delinquency can end in a forced sale.

sections.h2: What should a Norfolk owner with tax due do first?
sections.html:
Start by getting the real number. A payoff from the Treasurer beats an estimate from a bill that may be several months old.

  • Call the Treasurer's office or use the eBilling portal to confirm which quarters are open.
  • Ask the Assessor at 757-664-4732 how the current value was set if you think it is too high.
  • Ask the Department of Human Services at 757-823-1130 whether you qualify for real estate tax relief.
  • Tell the title company about any nuisance abatement lien, since the Treasurer collects those too.

If you want to skip repairs and showings, we can make a written cash offer on a Norfolk house as is, and the title company pays the tax from the proceeds.

faqs.q: What is the Norfolk real estate tax due date?
faqs.a: Norfolk bills quarterly, with payments due September 30, December 5, March 31 and June 5. The Treasurer mails bills at least 30 days before each date. City Council sets the dates and rates each year, so check your current bill.

faqs.q: Who do I call about my Norfolk assessment?
faqs.a: Call the City Assessor's office at 757-664-4732 for questions about value. To schedule an informal appeal with an appraiser, call 757-823-1343 after your April notice arrives.

faqs.q: When is the Norfolk Board of Review deadline?
faqs.a: The city code says appeals go to the Board of Review by the last business day in May. Late appeals can still be heard by the assessor, but the Board will not take them until the following year. File one application per parcel with an original and five copies.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Norfolk house if I owe property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. Virginia puts the tax lien first, so the unpaid amount comes out of the sale proceeds at closing and the treasurer releases the lien. Ask for a payoff figure before you sign anything.

faqs.q: Does Norfolk have an auction for unpaid tax?
faqs.a: Yes. The Treasurer's page lists an online-only public auction of parcels with unpaid real estate tax, sold under Va. Code 58.1-3975. Selling before a parcel reaches that stage keeps you in control of the price and the timing.
